first.rationale: The two observed declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which are causally linked: onboarding completion feeds activation. memory_86 and memory_31 both support onboarding/signup simplification, and memory_31 reports a durable first-week activation lift rather than a transient bump, so this direction addresses both symptoms with one experiment. I verify memory_86 and memory_31 because they are the direct basis for the intended action and because memory_31 is the oldest record (day 12) with the strongest durability claim \u\u2014 durability claims decay and deserve source-checking before a committed slot. memory_73 explicitly warns that promotional pricing, while the intuitive counter to the competitor's entry pricing, materially reduced 30-day retention and should not be generalized; under a sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective that is the wrong lever, so I do not spend verification budget re-litigating a memory whose own record already carries the caveat. memory_57 (referrals) and memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) are plausible but address neither declining metric. Downstream value risk: simplifying onboarding by cutting fields removes qualification signal, which can raise raw activation while lowering the quality of accounts that reach the funnel \u\u2014 the metric that improves is not the metric the objective names. I will therefore instrument on qualified-revenue and 30/60-day retention, not completion rate alone. Residual uncertainty: the inherited records are conclusions, not data; the prior lifts came from a pre-competitor market and may not transfer, and it is possible the current declines stem from a mix shift toward the competitor's price-sensitive segment rather than from onboarding friction at all. Standard experiment scale with a holdout, not a broad rollout.
